label: exploratory, dev only: labels by Claude (four Claude subagents per run, an LLM's, not a person's), blind, by the same rules and sheets

per_problem.after_note: 'adding more cutting minutes would not improve profit' is false: profit here is 0.4 x cutting minutes used. Enumerated: 1 to 4 more cutting minutes keep 1000 (20x+15y moves in steps of 5), but 5 more give 1002 (81 onions, 59 carrots). Borderline only in that it likely paraphrases a one-unit test.

Says to 'devote all 120 acres' before taking it back ('no, plant 50'); the optimum plants only 50 acres of watermelons (spraying binds) and leaves 70 unplanted (the facts; checked by enumerating the LP's vertices). Counted under the take-back decision; 120 itself is labeled correct as the farm's acreage.

Borderline, not counted: '$0.075 per extra budget dollar' is the model's shadow price, and the model fixes the GIC floor at $3,000; under the problem's '30% of his money' an extra dollar would add about $0.0585 (0.3*0.02 + 0.7*0.075). That's the formulation's reading, not a misstatement of the solution.
Both readings of easing the 55% share lower the water: by one unit of its own (0.55a - 0.45p <= 1) or to 54%, each gives 318 < 324; min anti-inflammatory >= 49 gives 316 (enumerated).

False: says gas 'would improve if the flower requirement were ... raised by one unit'. Raising it to 131 tightens it; enumerating whole cars and trucks, the optimum stays 212 (10 cars + 8 trucks still deliver 132). Only lowering it to 129 improves it (208: 11 cars, 7 trucks). Likely a slip for 'loosened', but as written it is a direction error. Also checked: dropping the flower rule -> 10, dropping cars>trucks -> 206, that rule at >=2 or >=0 -> 212 (true as stated).

Borderline wording, not counted: 'allowing one more unit of mineral would also help' is true read as loosening the >= 60 requirement by one (enumerated: >= 59 gives F=2, J=7, sugar 116 < 121) but would be false read as requiring 61 (121 unchanged); 'allowing' points to the loosening. Other claims enumerated true: drop mineral 98; drop the twice rule 114, loosen it 121; drop or loosen hydration 121.

Borderline. 'Relaxing [the 25% salmon cap] by one unit would lower fat' is true in the constraint's own unit (one salmon lunch over the share, 0.75s - 0.25b <= 1: fat 102 at 3 salmon, 6 bison) but false read as a 26% cap (fat stays 107). 'One unit' isn't worded as a share gap and is the unit the explanation also uses for the carb target, so I read it in the constraint's units. The cap does limit (dropping it gives 82). 'Raising the carb target by one unit wouldn't help' is true (181 g raises fat to 120; 179 g leaves 107), though raising is a tightening. All enumerated.

Borderline. 'Making that requirement looser would not help' is false as stated: enumerated, loosening demand by 1 to 299 sets keeps 13 lines, but a demand of 6,000 or less allows 12 large lines (312 employees). True only for a small (e.g. one-unit) loosening, likely what was meant.

Borderline no: 'the ratio rule's effect on loosening is unclear from the solution' is a hedge, not a false claim. Checked by enumeration: private - 2*commercial = -1 (or >= -1) gives 44, = +1 gives 46; the traveler requirement at 3499 or 3501 stays 45; dropping either constraint improves (0; 20), as stated.

Borderline. 'it is the only fully used constraint' is false: the 300-bucket supply (the buckets bound) is fully used too (300 buckets) and it limits: 301 buckets give 3,409 (enumerated). Borderline because that supply is a variable bound, not a listed constraint, and the facts list only the ratio as binding.

Borderline. 'Loosening the orders rule would not help by itself' is false as stated: enumerated, loosening it by 1 to 37 orders keeps 1370, but 812 orders allow 26 bike + 10 car = 1340. True for a one-unit loosening, likely what was meant. Also borderline (not needed for the yes): '0.1 of bike-share margin' is in trip units; a share reading would be false (26/37 = 70.27%).

Not a share gap: '0.8 of slack' on the boat-share rule is its slack in trip units (share is 37.0%). Both one-unit loosening claims check out by enumeration (boat share +1 gives 1860; product -1 keeps 1960).

'The solution would be worse without that limit' is reversed: dropping the heat limit raises the maximum excitement from 35 to 63 (1 force, 12 hydraulics), and loosening it by one unit gives 40 (enumerated every integer point). The clause before it, that the heat limit holds the result back, is true.

Borderline no: 'one extra wheel wouldn't help' is true (41 wheels still give 240; every toy uses an even number of wheels, enumerated); the stated reason ('a fraction of a wheel') is loose but not false. Two extra wheels would give 265.

Borderline no: 'the cap is the limit that matters most' is a judgment; its stated reason is true (a 6-bus cap -> 2220, while the worker requirement at 249 or 251 doesn't lower cost: 2250, 2300). Dropping the worker requirement saves more (0, vs 720 without the cap), so 'most' depends on the measure; not counted.

Borderline no: 'the worker supply is the real limit' does not deny other limits; the 8-truck-B minimum (a bound) also limits (dropping it gives 2,000 with 50 A and 0 B, enumerated), which the explanation omits but does not contradict.

Both readings of relaxing the expert share by one unit are true: 0.9E - 0.1A >= -1 or a 9% share each give 19,500 < 19,700. 'Adding more land to the requirement would not help' is true (a tightening; 5,001 m2 leaves 19,700). Enumerated.
Both readings of relaxing the 60% glove share lower the minutes: one unit of its own gives 8.2, a 59% share 8.35, against 8.5; 19 pills gives 8.15 (enumerated).

False: 'The two drink-mix rules do limit the result, even though they are not fully used up' - the 'more cappuccino than coffee' rule has slack 0 (2 - 1 = 1, binding), so it is fully used. The next sentence takes it back ('is fully used'), which still counts. Its limit claims check out by enumeration: dropping that rule -> 0; dropping or loosening the 30% rule -> 4; milk and cream changes leave 10.

'The 40% cap on XYZ's share ... has 0.2 left over' gives the cap's slack in its own units (servings: 0.4*18 - 7 = 0.2) worded as a share gap; XYZ's share is 7/18 = 38.9%, 1.1 points under 40% (not 0.2 points, nor 0.2 = 20 points), so the share reading is false. Borderline only in that no unit is stated. Its other claims check out by enumeration: drop the cap 30, loosen it by one 46; drop vitamin 39, loosen it 47; drop fiber or the 3-serving minimum 47.

Borderline no: 'raising it by one router wouldn't [improve]' holds either way: raising the requirement to 501 worsens it to 113, and relaxing it to 499 keeps 108 (enumerated); the whole-numbers reason fits only the relaxing reading. '0.8 of slack' on the 20% rule is its slack in driver units, not worded as a share gap (share is 25%).
Borderline wording, not false: 'making it one unit stricter wouldn't help' is true (7,001 trout leaves $1000), and loosening by one leaves $1000 too (enumerated).

Borderline, the weakest yes. 'loosening the ratio wouldn't reduce the count further' is false as stated: enumerated, small >= 3*large - k keeps 18 for k = 1 to 6 (and ratios down to 1.84), but k = 7 (or a ratio of 1.83) gives 17 (6 large, 11 small). True for a one-unit or moderate loosening. 'Adding more cars to the requirement' is a tightening (81 cars give 19), so that part is true.
'Raising the gas requirement's limit would not improve the result' is true either way: raising it gives 252, lowering it by one leaves 251 (enumerated).

'adding one more method ... would raise the total' is false: requiring one more method (101) lowers the maximum to 190,600 (64 escalators, 37 elevators), enumerated; only relaxing the requirement to 99 raises it (194,200). Likely a garbled one-unit relaxation, but as worded it states the wrong direction. The electricity half is true (801 units give 193,800).
'Adding one more unit of vitamin would not help' is true either way: 101 or 99 units both leave 49 (enumerated); relaxing hydration by one gives 46 and dropping vitamin gives 42, as stated.

Borderline, not counted: 'loosening the lactose limit by one unit would also help' is true in the constraint's own units (-0.1J + 0.9M <= 1: J=15, M=2, sugar 156 < 173, enumerated) but would be false read as an 11% cap (173 unchanged); 'one unit' isn't worded as a share. Other claims enumerated true: drop hydration 143, loosen it 173; drop lactose 42; drop vitamins 173.
